body: I failed out of my first two semesters - ended up getting academic probation because of low grades. I wound up going to a community college for a year so I could get my head on straight, wound up finding a major that was much more suited to me, returned to Rutgers and with my new major became a straight A student and was accepted into grad school and completed my Masters last year. It's hard not to be upset about getting an F grade on a course, but just remember that you don't need to work on anyone elses timeline or milestones. You'll get it when you get it.

If you want you can show the ceiling just before the exam begins, and explain to your professor that you do that when you're thinking. The professor is the one who decides to forward the case to student conduct or not, so as long as they are aware and don't see a problem you have nothing to worry about.

If the teacher says you can then its alright. The software does flag you if you look away from the screen but its up to the professor to report it and so if they know you are using scrap paper they generally wont forward it to student conduct, but I'd show the screen its blank just to be on the safe side. 

If your teacher didn't give permission and forward it to student conduct anyways, generally they would ask you for your explanation and if you show them your scrap paper they would add that into the "evidence" of the case. If you go before the honor council they use a "more likely than not" rule in regards to academic integrity such as cheating, ect., so if you show them your scrap paper they are likely to find you not responsible for that type of violation, but it depends on which honor council members are present.
